routes.label: registration at the constituency's registering office, the card collected there two weeks later

note: St Vincent and the Grenadines' national identification card comes with registration by the Electoral Office for persons of 18 and over: one registers at the constituency's registering office with a birth certificate, is photographed there, and collects the card there two weeks later (Searchlight, 17 July 2009, on the card made with Canadian Bank Note). The fee and the card's term weren't found; the Electoral Office's and the Government's sites refuse this client. Tried again 2026-10-29: a search of the Electoral Office's registration notices found no fee. Tried again 2026-10-30: a search for the card's fee or a replacement fee found only the Searchlight report and Electoral Office notices without a fee; electoral.gov.vc and gov.vc gave no answer to this client. The Electoral Office's own page of registration requirements (read 2026-11-03): one registers from 18, at the registration centres it sets up in each constituency (its Kingstown office for emergencies only), with a birth certificate, and the card is issued on registration; a card expires (an expired card means registering again), with no term given; a lost card is reprinted six months after it's reported, with a temporary card meanwhile (not modelled). It gives no fee, and the two weeks rest on Searchlight.

sources.title: Searchlight (St Vincent), Registration for new ID cards begins (17 July 2009)
sources.said: Come this November, the majority of persons eighteen years and older in St. Vincent and the Grenadines should be registered owners of the new national identification card. ... When going to register, Findlay-Scrubb said persons should take along their birth certificates. Photographs will be taken at the registering office in their constituency. Two weeks after registration, persons can collect their new identification cards at the place where they registered.

sources.title: Electoral Office, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Registration Requirements
sources.said: A person seeking to be registered should: Have attained the age of eighteen (18) years on the date on which he/she applies to be registered as a voter. ... Where should one go to get registered At the registration centres set up by the Electoral Office in the respective Constituency. At the Electoral Office in Kingstown (emergency only) ... For Vincentians (by birth) Original copy of Birth certificate ... NB: When a person gets registered, his/her name is added to the voters' list and a national identification card is issued to the person. ... A reprint of the ID card will be made and issued six (6) months after the report was received. ... (c) A persons who is eligible to be re-registered, whose card is expired should go to be registered
